title: U.S. House · Michigan's 8th District
area: Mid-Michigan, including Bay City, Saginaw and Flint (Bay, Saginaw and Genesee counties).

context.text: Incumbent Kristen McDonald Rivet (D) advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed with 104,752 votes. Thomas J. Smith (R) won a contested Republican primary with 50.4% of the vote.

summary.text: Kristen McDonald Rivet is the Democratic incumbent, seeking a second term. Before Congress she worked in education and early-childhood policy, served on the Bay City Commission and represented the 35th District in the Michigan Senate. According to her official biography, her priorities include cutting taxes for working and middle-class families and lowering costs for groceries, housing, prescription drugs and child care.

background.text: Born in 1970 in Portland, Michigan, per Wikipedia. According to her official biography, she was raised in a small farm town, where her father worked in construction and her mother stayed home, and she and her sisters were the first generation in the family to attend college.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from Michigan State University (1992) and a master's degree in education and public administration from the University of Michigan-Flint.

Began her career in early-childhood and education policy, including as executive director of Michigan Head Start, chief of staff of the Michigan Department of Education and vice president of The Skillman Foundation, according to her official biography.
Later worked as vice president of Michigan Future, Inc., president and CEO of Greater Midland, Inc., and chief strategy officer of the Michigan Health Improvement Alliance.
Held local office in Bay City, first on the city's Charter Commission and then on the Bay City Commission.

Elected to the Michigan Senate (District 35) in November 2022, defeating Annette Glenn (R), and served 2023 to 2025; she was assistant majority floor leader and served on committees including Appropriations and Education and Career Readiness.
Won Michigan's 8th District in 2024 after the retirement of Rep. Dan Kildee, defeating Paul Junge (R), and took office in January 2025.
In the U.S. House, serves on the Agriculture Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and was elected Freshman Leadership Representative to the New Democratic Coalition.
According to her official biography, lives in Bay City with her husband, Joseph, and has six children. She advanced unopposed from the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Investing in workforce training so Michiganders can access high-wage jobs.
priorities.quote: Michigan needs more high-wage jobs. Kristen will make sure we invest in our workforce to prepare Michiganders for the jobs of tomorrow because while college isn't for everyone, good-paying jobs should be.
She will also be steadfast in protecting our hard-earned freedoms and security, including defending the right to abortion, and keeping guns out of dangerous hands.

positions.summary: Campaigns on defending the right to abortion.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Thomas J. Smith

summary.text: Thomas J. Smith is the Republican nominee, a retired General Motors engineer who co-owns a salsa company. He won the August 2026 Republican primary with about half the vote even though he had suspended his campaign in mid-July, and his name remained on the ballot because ballots had already been printed. His campaign website describes his approach as conservative leadership guided by the Constitution, faith and freedom.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Kettering University and a graduate degree from Michigan State University.
Worked as an engineer at General Motors before retiring, according to news reports.
Is a small business owner who co-owns a salsa company, according to news reports.
Ran in the 2026 Republican primary for Michigan's 8th District against Trump-endorsed Amir Hassan and Al Lemmo. He suspended his campaign in mid-July and endorsed Lemmo, but remained on the ballot.

Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 50.4% of the vote, ahead of Hassan (about 33%) and Lemmo, and is the party's nominee against Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet. In a statement he said he was "humbled and honored that Republicans have chosen me to take the fight to Kristen McDonald Rivet."

candidates.researchNotes: Smith's campaign website did not load readable content, and he has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, so no verifiable statements of his positions or priorities were found.

candidates.name: Jim Casha

summary.text: Jim Casha is the Green Party candidate for Michigan's 8th District. Little biographical information is available in public sources.

background.text: Advanced from the Green Party convention on April 25, 2026, and is on the November 3 general-election ballot.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, public statements, or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response found.

candidates.name: C. Mia Pettus

summary.text: C. Mia Pettus is the Libertarian Party candidate for Michigan's 8th District. Describing herself as a former police officer and independent researcher, she is running on constitutional limits, government transparency and privacy protections.

background.text: Describes herself as a Michigan resident, Christian and mother who is a former City of Philadelphia certified police officer, a former Department of Defense Navy civilian federal police officer, an independent researcher and the publisher of the PALS Report on Substack.
Says her run for Congress was also shaped by personal experience including building a business, financial hardship, parenting a child with a disability and periods of housing instability.
Advanced from the Libertarian Party convention on June 28, 2026.

candidates.name: Kathy Goodwin

summary.text: Kathy Goodwin is the Working Class Party candidate for Michigan's 8th District. In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as shaped by the Flint, Saginaw and Bay City area.

background.text: In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, said the Flint, Saginaw and Bay City area formed her and that she attended public school in Montrose, outside Flint.
Advanced from the Working Class Party convention on June 6, 2026.
